strings.name: Mary-Claire King
strings.summary: King moved from mathematics to genetics, studying human evolution and inherited disease. In 1990 her team mapped susceptibility in some breast-cancer families to chromosome 17, paving the way for other teams to clone BRCA1. She also used genetic markers and DNA analysis to help identify abducted Argentine children and their relatives. A Berkeley and Washington professor honored by the Lasker awards, she connected prevention, basic research and human rights work.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through November 13, 2026; not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: Advanced inherited breast-cancer susceptibility and BRCA1 mapping research, and applied genetics to human rights identification.
strings.facts.f1.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.f1.value: Chicago area, United States; born February 27, 1946.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Mapping inherited susceptibility
strings.highlights.h1.text: Her team’s 1990 linkage analysis supported the BRCA1 locus, distinct from gene cloning by other teams in 1994.
strings.facts.f2.label: Education
strings.facts.f2.value: Mathematics degree, Carleton; genetics PhD, UC Berkeley (1973).
strings.highlights.h2.title: Genetics and human rights
strings.highlights.h2.text: Helped develop kinship methods to establish identities of abducted Argentine children and victims of human rights abuses.
strings.timeline.t1.title: NYU honorary degree
strings.timeline.t1.text: Received an honorary science doctorate for genetics and human rights contributions, reported by Washington in June.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Princess of Asturias Award
strings.timeline.t2.text: Received the technical and scientific research prize for disease genetics and human rights contributions.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Lasker special achievement award
strings.timeline.t3.text: Received the Lasker–Koshland Special Achievement Award in Medical Science.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Moved to Washington
strings.timeline.t4.text: Moved from Berkeley to Seattle to continue medical genetics and genome research.
strings.timeline.t5.title: BRCA1 linkage mapping
strings.timeline.t5.text: Her team linked inherited breast-cancer risk in some families to a chromosome 17 region.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Identification work in Argentina
strings.timeline.t6.text: Worked with grandmothers’ organizations and scientific colleagues to establish kinship for abducted children.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Genetics doctorate
strings.timeline.t7.text: Completed Berkeley doctoral research, studying human and chimpanzee evolution with adviser Wilson.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Born in the Chicago area
strings.timeline.t8.text: Grew up in the American Midwest, later studying mathematics before turning to genetics.
